title: 34 kW Micro Hydropower Plant Design
summary: A completed rural-electrification design study for Kewai Village, Naran, covering the water-to-wire system and its environmental and economic feasibility.
overview: This Complex Engineering Project studied a 34 kW micro hydropower scheme for rural electrification in Kewai Village, Naran, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The work connects resource and load assessment with turbine-generator selection, civil arrangements, electrical distribution and implementation planning. It is a design study; the illustrations do not establish a constructed or commissioned plant.
approach: Assessed available head and flow alongside the village load requirements.
Selected a cross-flow turbine and a 35 kW induction generator for the proposed scheme.
Developed the intake, penstock, powerhouse, control, transformer and distribution-network scope.
Considered costing, implementation planning, environmental impact and economic feasibility.
outcomes: Completed the academic plant-design study at a 34 kW design capacity.
Estimated annual generation of approximately 146,000 kWh and payback below two years. These are design estimates, not measured operating results.
The completed deliverable is an academic design study; construction and commissioning are not part of this record.
